In [[mathematics]], especially in the area of [[algebraic topology]] known as [[stable homotopy theory]], the '''Adams filtration''' and the '''Adams–Novikov filtration''' allow a stable homotopy group to be understood as built from layers, the ''n''th layer containing just those maps which require at most ''n'' auxiliary spaces in order to be a composition of homologically trivial maps.  These filtrations, named after [[Frank Adams]] and [[Sergei Novikov (mathematician)|Sergei Novikov]], are of particular interest because the [[Adams spectral sequence|Adams (–Novikov) spectral sequence]] converges to them.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.math.rochester.edu/faculty/doug/mypapers/|title=mypapers|website=people.math.rochester.edu}}</ref><ref>https://scholar.harvard.edu/files/rastern/files/adamsspectralsequence.pdf&ved=2ahUKEwjI-JDstJOEAxU4WEEAHThuAOI4ChAWegQIGxAB&usg=AOvVaw3_Ga18v-jBF18FS-U4KgPV</ref>

==Definition==
The [[group (mathematics)|group]] of stable homotopy classes <math>[X,Y]</math> between two [[spectrum (homotopy theory)|spectra]] ''X'' and ''Y'' can be given a [[filtration (mathematics)|filtration]] by saying that a map <math>f\colon X\to Y</math> has filtration ''n'' if it can be written as a composite of maps 
:<math>X=X_0 \to  X_1 \to \cdots \to X_n = Y</math> 
such that each individual map <math>X_i\to X_{i+1}</math> induces the zero map in some fixed [[homology theory]] ''E''. If ''E'' is ordinary mod-''p'' [[singular homology|homology]], this filtration is called the '''Adams filtration''', otherwise the '''Adams–Novikov filtration'''.
